disposition: Research-only minor age-boundary discrepancy; other checked source descriptions have affirmative primary support. No issue promotion while exact federal legislative vehicle remains unverified.
actual_read_extent: All five physical pages of SG2609210003, including July 2026 body-date marker, page 1 EU-plan summary, pages 3–4 requests and final policy context.
Original Commission COM(2025)1024 physical pages 8–10, including complete target list and footnote 55; not full Commission document.
assessment: The primary target list starts at age 25, whereas the author gives 26 on page 1 and over 26 on page 3. The boundary discrepancy is concrete, with an ordinary transcription or age-wording slip as an obvious benign explanation.

The source sets population-coverage targets by 2035, rather than a directly binding clinical screening obligation. Footnote 55 leaves definitions to future protocol and programme design. Preserve those distinctions.

The author itself gives the 65–90 percent coverage range on page 1, which qualifies an isolated reading of the later annual-check sentence. Do not promote a separate universal-screening allegation by omitting that context.

The author’s own page 4 request is broader: annual check-ups from 18. Correcting the EU lower boundary by one year does not invalidate that independent preference or establish its clinical benefit. Materiality is minor at most; direction is unknown and should not be forced true.

The text calls for national reform and discusses GeDIG and ApoVWG among several measures, but an exact federal bill version specifically addressed by this July position has not been established. Register filing alone does not resolve that gate.
additional_primary_read_extent: Original OECD 2025 cardiovascular report physical pages 105 and 112, complete relevant economic-burden passage and Table 2.2 including column units and notes.
Original German country health profile 2023 physical page 11, complete prevention-versus-treatment mortality discussion, figure explanation and methodology.
Original Commission plan physical page 12, complete tobacco taxation passage and footnotes.
negative_review_addendum: The OECD source itself gives Germany 903 as the highest listed EU per-capita cardiovascular societal-cost estimate. Table 2.2 explicitly labels the per-capita unit as purchasing-power adjusted; preserve that unit and the 2021-euro basis when explaining the number. No refutation of the reported ranking or supported rounded figure is established. Do not relabel it as a current nominal expenditure or public budget amount.

The country profile supports 157 per 100,000 for prevention-avoidable mortality in 2020, identifies ischaemic heart disease among leading causes and separately gives 81 for treatable mortality. The author’s broad avoidable wording can reasonably refer to the prevention subset in its prevention-policy context. No contradictory mortality result established.

The original Commission plan expressly attributes around 40% of the EU smoking decline over the past decade to taxation. This supports the source-description claim. This review has not independently replicated the underlying impact analysis or established causal certainty.
